approach.method_basis: The reference this node measures is the lineage's current best algorithm: a graph genetic algorithm whose oracle calls are chosen by Gaussian-process Thompson sampling, with one stall reflex on top. Every round it breeds a fresh field of 160 molecules from a 64-member elite, drawing breeding parents mostly from the top score quantiles and building each child either by joining connected fragments of two parents, sometimes with one further edit, or by a short chain of atom, bond and ring edits. It rejects duplicates, and also any child that would introduce a sulfur environment its scored parents do not already carry. A Gaussian process trained only on the molecules scored so far in that same run, using count-based Morgan fingerprints and a Tanimoto-type similarity, predicts the whole fresh field; ten correlated posterior samples then each buy their best still-available candidate, and those ten molecules are scored. The reflex is the part earlier work added: after three consecutive rounds with no new best score, only the forty candidates with the highest predicted mean remain eligible to be bought, until a round improves again. Two independent random streams drive a run - one makes every breeding decision, the other draws only the posterior samples - and the reflex itself consumes no randomness. On the recorded runs it governed 88 of 435 rounds, in 13 of the 15 runs, and two of the runs never stalled at all.
approach.novelty: This node adds no search behaviour at all. It is the placebo the stall reflex has never had: a measurement of how far the score moves when only luck changes, inside exactly the rounds the reflex governs. In each round in which the eligibility restriction is active, and nowhere else, it draws one number from the breeding stream and throws it away before anything else in that round happens, so the breeding decisions of that round and later ones consume different random draws while every rule, probability, threshold and the selector's own random numbers stay exactly as they are. The earlier placebo on this same algorithm re-drew in every round, which charges luck over the whole run and destroys the two unusually high results this Parent's score leans on; the two gated placebos were drawn on the previous algorithm, which had no reflex, and perturbed the selector's stream rather than breeding. Confining the perturbation to the stalled rounds leaves the two runs that never stall reproduced number for number, so the lucky result they carry cannot contaminate the reading, and it leaves four fifths of all rounds untouched. What comes out is the band a reader needs in order to say whether the reflex's own apparent gain is larger than luck inside its own regime. Siblings cannot supply it: they each changed a rule - a mixture predictor, a session-calibrated spread, greedy allocation, a doubled field, releasing or holding the restriction - or removed a dormant branch and reproduced the Parent exactly, so none of them measured confined departure alone.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent is the formal L01 Anchor n-61b9b3bfb40d, and the behaviour that limits it is not an algorithmic one: the single element it is named for cannot be read on it. Its one positive result is +0.010577 against its mask-free Parent n-1744a1494180 (panel 0.607030; seed macros 0.649701/0.585234/0.586156; paired seed deltas +0.006603/+0.022061/+0.003067), and that element - the stall-time top-forty eligibility restriction, given its own identity m-61b9b3bfb40d by review 19 - is recorded in the frozen catalog on this Anchor with needs_evidence true and an evidence list of length zero, one of eleven contribution gaps standing on this Anchor. The two bounds that do exist price something else. (i) n-515ab49db6e0, the only law-free reference ever drawn on this host, discards one breeding draw in every announced batch: it realized -0.020452 with fifteen-cell SD 0.067837 and band [-0.055482, +0.014579]. That band is ungated, so it charges path departure over all 435 announced batches, loses both of the Anchor's fragile seed-0 cells (deco_hop 0.856148 to 0.607697 and sitagliptin_mpo 0.765861 to 0.670248, together -0.022937 of a panel against +0.002868 averaged over the other thirteen cells), and even puts the two deco_hop sessions that never stall into the regime; the Anchor's margin is less than a third of that half-width largely because the exposure class is wrong. (ii) n-c4c934fd6a68 retains the whole restriction code and is byte-identical to the mask-free removal n-f04cec6ab705 in all fifteen trajectory files and all fifteen cells (both panels 0.480136, mask_binding false in 435 of 435 batches), so at the greedy destination the element is worth exactly zero and the -0.010577 between those two deltas (-0.126894 against -0.116317) is the Anchor-minus-Parent baseline reappearing rather than a contribution. Re-reading the Anchor's own receipts shows why the gated class is the one that is missing: an independent recount of its stall_regime_state events over all fifteen sessions reproduces 88 restricted of 435 announced batches, 29 episodes, 13 of 15 sessions, with deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 never triggering (per-session first restricted batch: seed 0 zaleplon_mpo 4, median_2 4, sitagliptin_mpo 12, drd2_docking 23; seed 1 sitagliptin_mpo 7, zaleplon_mpo 8, deco_hop 15, drd2_docking 15, median_2 18; seed 2 zaleplon_mpo 6, median_2 8, sitagliptin_mpo 17, drd2_docking 19). The mask therefore acts in one fifth of the batches while the only law-free scale on this host is measured over all of them, so every mask-confined contrast still borrows the mask-free Parent's two gated realizations, -0.001735 (n-47993ce5d053) and +0.007747 (n-843b25e73dee), whose two-point spread 0.009482 is itself the floor of this Anchor's registered reading rule. h-2fa4b3d0e8726724 names a trigger-matched reference as one of the only two measurements that can price this element and h-122694bed089edde records that this Anchor has none.
hypothesis: Trigger-matched law-free path divergence on the stall-masked Anchor. No law, probability, threshold, rule or constant changes anywhere. In Evolution.suggest, after the inherited stall-state block has computed this batch's regime from the inherited K=3 counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches and logged stall_regime_state, and before the GP fit, the probe update and the batch's first breeding draw, draw exactly one value with random() from the Evolution's own seeded random.Random(seed) generator - the generator GraphOperators shares - and discard it, if and only if that same batch's inherited restrict_top_mean is not None, which is exactly the condition under which the top-forty eligibility restriction is passed to the allocator for that batch. Outside the restricted regime nothing extra is consumed. That generator drives quantile parent and rank sampling, the crossover-versus-mutation and finishing coins, walk length and every operator, site and element draw, so from the discard onward every breeding decision consumes different pseudo-random words and the realized path departs from the Anchor inside the restricted regime only. Everything that decides anything stays exactly as inherited: the eligibility rule itself with K=3, M=40 of the unchanged 160-member pool, the (-posterior mean, pool index) ordering, the per-pick mask update and restoration on the first improving batch; the accepted-only chronological count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto posterior with its 0.05 noise SD, adaptive mean and population-SD normalization, full covariance and float64 Cholesky jitter ladder; the single (10, 160) standard-normal array drawn from the separately seeded torch generator, its consumption order and the sequentially masked argmax pricing with its tie rule and numerical fallback; the sulfur gate, canonical identity admission, both duplicate scopes, greedy-64 retention, quantile breeding, the continuation law, the seven operator families at unchanged weights and connected-fragment crossover at 0.45 with its finishing edit. No decision reads the discarded value. The claim is a measurement, not a gain: the complete matched fifteen-cell panel delta against the Anchor is what law-free path departure costs when it is confined to the batches the mask governs, with 347 of the Anchor's 435 announced batches and both of its never-stalling deco_hop sessions untouched by construction.

finding_summary.headline: Stall-confined luck-only re-draw ran exactly and cost -0.0212; the Anchor's +0.0106 sits above this gated band, but its 0.0235 width leaves it uncalibrated
finding_summary.insights:
The trigger-matched luck scale this Anchor lacked now exists, and it does not establish the stall restriction. By the registered position clause the Anchor's +0.0106 lies above the gated band, but only because the band is centred on this draw's own loss of -0.021. Its half-width, 0.0235, is more than twice the gain, which under the rule's width clause leaves the element uncalibrated rather than supported. So this is not the first supported reading of the stall restriction, and one dependent realization supports no significance statement either way.

The sharper finding is where the luck lives. The Anchor's entire +0.0106 over its mask-free Parent comes from two sitagliptin cells, seed 0 (+0.0716) and seed 1 (+0.1445); the other 13 cells net -0.0038. A perturbation that changes no rule and touches only the stalled rounds, about one round in five, moved those same two cells by -0.1025 and -0.1575, more than the gain they carry. On the one task that carries the Anchor's gain, the endpoint swings by 0.10 to 0.16 depending on which random words the breeding draws consume inside the stall regime. The molecular report shows how. The Anchor's seed-0 run left an N-aryl anisole branch for a polyfluorinated non-aromatic ring and climbed to 0.766, while this run stayed on the anisole branch and plateaued at 0.663 after three improvements. Whether the restriction contributes anything on this host therefore turns on two cells that regime-confined luck alone moves by more than the claimed gain. Attributing it is left to Curate, with a revised interpretation of the Anchor.

Confining the perturbation to stalled rounds did not shrink the average cost of leaving the Anchor's path. The gated loss (-0.0212) is almost the ungated one (-0.0205), though the cell spread fell (0.046 against 0.068) and the deco_hop seed-0 jackpot was preserved by construction. The loss simply moved from deco_hop to sitagliptin. The Anchor's panel holds several luck-sensitive high cells, and which of them a departure loses depends on where it departs. Arms on this Anchor that act inside stalled rounds now have their own gated scale, which must not be pooled with the ungated band or with the two mask-free gated references.

Method diagnosis, from this node's trajectories and the molecular report, in three parts. First, late search re-prices a few skeletons. Distinct scaffolds per run are 116.4 (Anchor 117.5) but only 52.0 in the second half and 36.5 in the last 100 evaluations. After evaluation 150, 19% of accepted proposals (13.5% overall; Anchor 17.2% and 12.3%) scored exactly a value already seen in the same run. The tied endpoints show what these are: halogen-placement and halogen-identity variants of one skeleton that the objective cannot tell apart, for example three distinct drd2 molecules at exactly 0.973518, all halogen variants of the Anchor's best. A batch acquisition rule that penalizes redundancy against already-scored molecules, or proposal operators that edit skeletons rather than substituent identity, would stop spending a fifth of late oracle calls on such relabellings. Second, the surrogate ranks worst exactly where the stall restriction leans on it. Among a round's ten picks, the rank correlation between predicted mean and realized score averages 0.56 in unrestricted rounds but 0.43 in restricted ones (Anchor 0.55 and 0.39). Part of that drop is simply the narrower spread of predicted means among top-forty picks, but restricted rounds also add far less best-score gain per round (0.0053 against 0.0149 here; 0.0062 against 0.0157 on the Anchor). A stall response that trusts the posterior mean more just when it is least informative is weak by construction. A response that changes where proposals come from, such as a trust-region shift or restart scheme, or a surrogate refitted locally around the current basin, would target the actual problem. Third, the endpoint is a lottery: one discarded draw in a fifth of the rounds moved two sitagliptin cells by 0.10 and 0.16, because each run commits to a single basin early. A search scheme that keeps several independent sub-populations alive would reduce that variance.

By the route's own conditions no second draw and no sweep of the discard count, trigger or bar follows, so this measurement route stops here. Still open is whether the stall restriction contributes on this host at all. A handoff named two measurements able to price it; this trigger-matched reference has now returned a band too wide to calibrate it, which leaves a mask-confined variant on the Anchor's own path, together with Curate's revised interpretation of the Anchor.
finding_summary.results:
The placebo did exactly what it was built to do and nothing else. In all 15 runs it logged one discard record per round (435 in total) and threw away one breeding random number in exactly the 84 rounds in which that run's own stall reflex was active, and in none of the other 351. Each discard came after the round's stall check and before the model fit and the first breeding draw. The two deco_hop runs that never stall drew nothing and reproduced the Anchor's runs molecule for molecule and log record for log record, ending at exactly 0.856148 (seed 0) and 0.644234 (seed 2). In the other 13 runs, every scored molecule and every logged breeding, pool, selection and stall record before the first stalled round matched the Anchor's exactly: 2,160 of 4,500 scored molecules, including the 150 starting molecules, and 75,841 log records. The first stalled round fell where it did in the Anchor in all 13 runs, and each run left the Anchor's path right there, at the first breeding attempt of that round; the first different scored molecule came one to seven evaluations into that round. No rule moved. The selector's own random numbers matched the Anchor's bit for bit in all 4,350 picks, every round bred a full pool of 160, there were no fallbacks, and the stall counter, the top-forty restriction, the model fits, the sulfur gate, the duplicate checks and the operator, crossover and finishing rates all conformed to the inherited rules on the run's own records. Where both runs were unrestricted (317 rounds), the picks sat at the same places in the predicted-score and uncertainty rankings as the Anchor's (shift statistics -1.55 and +0.34 against a bound of 3.26).

After leaving, the runs went their own way: only 146 of the 2,329 molecules scored after the departure point (6.3%) also appear anywhere in the Anchor's same run. The stall reflex's own exposure drifted with the new paths, as the design allowed: 84 restricted rounds in 35 episodes against the Anchor's 88 in 29, with 13 rounds at restricted depth six or more against 19. Inside the restricted rounds no pick ever fell outside the top forty by predicted mean (840 picks, mean rank 11.2 against the Anchor's 11.7). Those rounds broke the stall 29 times in 84 (34.5%; Anchor 25 of 88) but added less best-score gain (0.445 against 0.547).

Scores: the panel mean was 0.585797 against the Anchor's 0.607030, a reference delta of -0.021233, with all three seed macros lower (-0.0291, -0.0294, -0.0052). Two cells rose, nine fell and four were identical: the two never-stalling deco_hop runs, plus drd2 and sitagliptin on seed 2, which re-reached the Anchor's exact scores with halogen-swapped analogues of its best molecules. In task order (zaleplon, deco_hop, drd2, median_2, sitagliptin) the cells moved: seed 0 -0.0383, 0, +0.0126, -0.0175, -0.1025; seed 1 +0.0132, -0.0016, -0.000005, -0.0011, -0.1575; seed 2 -0.0027, 0, 0, -0.0232, 0. Two sitagliptin cells carry most of the loss. Seed 0 ended at 0.6634 instead of 0.7659 and seed 1 at 0.4869 instead of 0.6444, together -0.0173 of the panel; the other 13 cells average -0.0045. Every exposed run still finished above its inherited pre-departure best.

The registered reading rule: the fifteen cell deltas have a spread of 0.045603, so the half-width is max(0.009482, 2 x 0.045603 / sqrt(15)) = 0.023549 and the gated band is -0.021233 plus or minus 0.023549, i.e. -0.044783 to +0.002316. The Anchor's +0.010577 over its mask-free Parent lies 0.008261 above the band's upper edge, so by the position clause it stands above this gated law-free scale. By the same rule's width clause, a half-width at or above about 0.010 leaves the element uncalibrated, and 0.023549 is well above that. For median_2 the band is -0.013938 plus or minus 0.010807 (-0.024745 to -0.003131), from cells -0.0175, -0.0011 and -0.0232. Protected task means: deco_hop 0.706851 against 0.707370 (-0.0005, inside its 0.02 margin), drd2_docking 0.988766 against 0.984572 (+0.0042, inside 0.03), zaleplon 0.428349 against 0.437595 (-0.0092, inside 0.02), and sitagliptin 0.590128 against 0.676784 (-0.0867, beyond its 0.02 margin); median_2 0.214892 against 0.228830.

molecular.headline: Halogen-heavy fused heteroaromatics, two of fifteen sessions identical to the Anchor's molecules; no node-level scaffold collapse, 116.4 vs 117.5 per session
molecular.overall_character: Across all 4,350 optimizer proposals (five objectives, seeds 0/1/2, 290 proposals plus ten shared initial records each) this node emits mid-sized, flat, heavily substituted heteroaromatics: 24.4-31.5 heavy atoms on average per objective, 3.2-4.4 rings of which 2.1-3.7 are aromatic, fsp3 0.16-0.37, and no charged atom anywhere (digest charged_rate 0.0 on all five). The digest counters agree with structural perception: ring_closure_rate 0.9690-0.9851 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9609-0.9759, so ring and aromatic content really is dense rather than a string artefact. Decoration is overwhelmingly halogen (halogen_rate 0.80-0.98 on four of five objectives) and the halogen lands on heteroatoms as readily as on carbon: 857 of 4,350 proposals contain an N-halogen bond and 157 an O-halogen bond, while not one of the 4,350 contains a CF3 group. QED means run 0.31-0.65 and SA scores 3.1-4.4, so the molecules sit at the edge of ordinary medicinal chemistry, pulled off it by reactive decoration: 241 nitroso, 258 thiocarbonyl, 120 peroxide O-O, 279 aminal, 79 alpha-halo ether, 29 allene and 7 acyl halide proposals. 2,539 of 4,350 carry at least one unassigned stereocentre and none is specified. Against the Parent Anchor n-61b9b3bfb40d the molecule sets are near-identical in bulk character: the Parent's 4,350 proposals hold 888 N-halogen, 241 nitroso, 2,578 unassigned-stereocentre and 98 six-or-fewer-heavy-atom molecules against this node's 857, 241, 2,539 and 116. Session-level structure: in deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 all 300 records are the Parent's molecules in the Parent's order, Top-1 0.856148 and 0.644234 reproduced exactly; in the other thirteen sessions the first differing molecule falls inside the ten evaluations of that session's first restricted batch in 13 of 13 cases (for example seed 0 zaleplon_mpo batch 4, evaluations 41-50, first difference at 41; seed 0 drd2_docking batch 23, first difference at 231), and after that the two paths share little chemistry - seed 0 zaleplon_mpo shares only 59 of 300 molecules with the Parent. I measured scaffold structure directly rather than by string uniqueness, and I do not reproduce a scaffold collapse. Mean distinct Bemis-Murcko scaffolds per session over the 290 optimizer proposals is 116.4 here against 117.5 for the Parent (the definition that reproduces the quoted 117.5 exactly), and generic (element- and bond-agnostic) frameworks are 72.3 for both. The 54.9-per-session figure matches a different window, not a different node: counting only the second half of each session (evaluations 151-300) gives 55.0 scaffolds for the Parent and 52.0 here, and the last 100 evaluations give 36.7 and 36.5. The collapse is therefore within-session and temporal, present in both nodes, not a loss this node introduced: diversity is spent early and the late budget is spent permuting substituents on a handful of surviving skeletons.

per_task.generated_character: Indole- and azaindole-2-carboxanilides, 24.4 heavy atoms on average, 3.16 rings of which 2.62 aromatic, fsp3 0.22, QED 0.61, SA 3.09. 677 of 870 proposals carry an amide and 671 an aryl halide; the 870 proposals cover 104 distinct ring systems but the top 87 only 9, most commonly benzene and pyridine. Late search is one analogue family: the last 50 evaluations of each seed (150 molecules) hold 40 scaffolds with 34 in the largest family and 58% in the top three. Nine of the twelve digest best molecules are the same methyl-dihydropyrrolo-indene carboxamide differing only in which halogen sits on the amide nitrogen and the side chain, all tied at 0.447848.
liabilities: N-halogen amides in 73 of the top 87 molecules, including the best molecule of the whole task at 0.4520
N-hydroxy amide (hydroxamic-type) decoration in 13 proposals, 3 of them in the top 87
peroxide O-O bonds appended to the aromatic core in 8 proposals
22 proposals of six or fewer heavy atoms, arriving as late as evaluation 268, that no oracle can reward
7 proposals with a bond drawn across an aromatic ring, giving a three- or four-membered all-aromatic ring
missing_features: no basic amine on any of the top 87 molecules (16 of 870 overall), so no ionisable centre is offered on this bicyclic series
no sulfonamide, nitrile or small polar heteroaryl replacement, although the objective's named reference chemotype is an acetamide-sulfonyl type
no CF3, OCF3 or other polyhalogenated carbon substituent anywhere in the 870 proposals
no saturated ring appended to the aromatic core: fsp3 stays 0.22 and only 2 proposals carry an 8-11-membered ring
no specified stereochemistry; 79 of 870 carry an unassigned stereocentre
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises with size and ring count and falls with polarity: the top 100 proposals average 24.7 heavy atoms, 3.43 rings, logP 4.18 and 0.60 H-bond donors, the bottom 100 average 18.4 heavy atoms, 2.23 rings, logP 3.00 and 1.48 donors. Amide presence rises 52 to 80 of 100 and N-halogen 19 to 78 of 100 from bottom to top, so the gradient is rewarding a lipophilic bicyclic amide of roughly the right mass, and the optimizer reaches it partly by N-halogenation rather than by real decoration. This node's seed-0 line topped out at 0.3852 against the Anchor's 0.4235 in the same session, the Anchor having kept a nicotinamide-type anilide where this node substituted thioethers.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Over 4,350 optimizer proposals read from this node's fifteen staging trajectory files, 857 molecules contain an N-halogen bond and 157 an O-halogen bond, while zero contain a CF3 group. The reliance is concentrated at the top: on one objective 73 of the 87 highest-scoring molecules carry an N-halogen amide and the single best molecule of that objective is one of them (CCc1c(C)cc2c(c1C)c(Br)c(C(=O)N(O)c1ccccn1)n2F), and on another 53 of 87 do, led by COc1ccccc1-n1cc2c(c1C1(C)CC(F)N1)c(=O)n(F)c(=N)n2F. One leader carries an aryl O-F hypofluorite and an alpha-chloro ether at once (O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator halogenates nitrogen and oxygen as freely as carbon and cannot build a polyhalogenated carbon substituent.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Halogen substitution is the cheapest edit in the operator set and is applied without regard to the element it lands on, so an objective that rewards halogen count is answered with bonds a chemist would not draw. A task-agnostic generator would treat heteroatom-halogen bond formation as its own rarely-valid operator class and supply the ordinary alternatives it currently cannot build at all: trifluoromethyl, difluoromethyl, trifluoromethoxy and geminal dihalides on carbon.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest reports charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five objectives over 870 proposals each, and structural perception of the same molecules finds 2,539 of 4,350 carrying at least one unassigned stereocentre. On the objective whose gradient most clearly rewards an ionisable amine, 493 of 870 proposals carry a basic amine, 84 of the 87 best do, and 834 of 870 have an undefined stereocentre; its best molecules (CC1(c2cccc(Cl)c2)NCCCCN1CCc1cc(CCN)cc(Br)c1N and CCc1cc(Br)cc(CCN2CCCNC2(C)c2cccc(Cl)c2)c1C) are each scored as a single unspecified diastereomer in an uncharged form.
transferable_gaps.gap: No charged species and no specified stereochemistry are ever emitted, even where the leaders are stereogenic amines.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation as used cannot express configuration or protonation state, so every sp3 centre the operators build is an undefined mixture and any surface sensitive to enantiomers, diastereomers or ionisation is being scored on an ambiguous structure. A task-agnostic generator would assign configuration when it creates a tetrahedral centre, carry it through every edit, and be able to propose a protonated or deprotonated form of a group it has just installed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Measured directly as Bemis-Murcko scaffolds rather than string uniqueness, each session's 290 optimizer proposals contain 116.4 distinct scaffolds on average, but the second half of each session (evaluations 151-300) contains only 52.0 and the last 100 only 36.5. Pooling three seeds, the final 50 evaluations per objective hold as few as 33 scaffolds with 28 molecules in the largest family and 49% in the top three, and on one objective nine of the twelve best molecules are one skeleton tied at exactly 0.447848, differing only in which halogen sits on the amide nitrogen and the side chain (Cc1c2c(cc3c1CN3C)C(C(=O)N(Br)c1ccc(CCBr)nc1)=C2, Cc1c2c(cc3c1CN3C)C(C(=O)N(F)c1ccc(CCF)nc1)=C2, COc1c2c(cc3c1CN3C)C(C(=O)N(F)c1ccc(CCF)nc1)=C2). The top-scoring decile of four of five objectives spans only 9 to 17 distinct ring systems.
transferable_gaps.gap: Scaffold diversity is spent early and the late budget only permutes peripheral substituents; the generator has no skeleton-level edit at comparable frequency.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Late search concentrates on substituent identity at a few peripheral heteroatoms, the cheapest edit available and the one least likely to move any score, so roughly half the evaluation budget re-prices one skeleton. A task-agnostic generator would need ring-skeleton, fusion-pattern and linker-length edits firing at a rate comparable to substituent swaps, and a novelty pressure defined on the scaffold rather than on the canonical string, so that two molecules differing only in a terminal halogen do not both consume an oracle call.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 116 of 4,350 proposals have six or fewer heavy atoms and 114 are ringless, spread across all five objectives (22, 27, 23, 13 and 31), and they arrive as late as evaluations 284, 286 and 293 of 300. They include a bare carbon atom, diatomics and small halogen species (C, C=C, FBr, ClNBr, CCF, SCS, FCCF, NOON, CCOOC). On one objective every such fragment scores the task floor of exactly 0.5 and on three others exactly 0.0.
transferable_gaps.gap: Deletion operators are unbounded below, so sub-pharmacophore fragments are proposed to the oracle instead of being repaired.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Atom, bond and ring deletion have no lower bound, so a measurable slice of every fixed evaluation budget is spent on species no oracle can reward and which carry no information for the surrogate. A task-agnostic generator would bound deletion by a minimum heavy-atom or ring count, or route a molecule that falls below it back through a growth operator before it is proposed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4,350 proposals there are 241 nitroso, 258 thiocarbonyl, 120 peroxide O-O, 279 aminal, 79 alpha-halo ether, 302 N-N single bond, 238 N-O single bond, 29 allene and 7 acyl halide molecules. These are not confined to the discarded tail: on one objective 48 of the 87 best molecules are nitroso-bearing, including its best-scoring final molecule (COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2) and a thiocarbonyl ester analogue of it (CC(=O)c1c(C)c(C(N=O)Nc2cc3c(N=O)cc2-3)c2c(c1CCOC=S)C=N2), and 44 of another objective's 87 best contain an aminal.
transferable_gaps.gap: There is no stability vocabulary: reactive and short-lived groups are attached to otherwise reasonable scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Admission currently tests valence, canonical novelty and one narrow inherited element rule, and nothing else about chemical stability, so the cheapest way to add polarity is to add a group that would not survive isolation. A task-agnostic generator would classify the local environment each edit creates against a general reactivity vocabulary covering N-O, O-halogen, N-halogen, N-N, N-S, peroxide, acyl halide, aminal and cumulated double bonds, and either refuse those edits or price them before spending an oracle call.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 156 of 4,350 proposals contain a ring of four or fewer atoms every one of whose atoms is aromatic, that is a bond drawn across the interior of a benzene ring, and they reach the leaders: 20 of one objective's top 87 and 17 of another's. Examples include COc1c(OC)c2c3[nH]c(C(=O)Nc4ccc(F)cc4)c2c3c1OC and CCOC(=O)c1ccc(O)c2c1-c1c3c(c(-c4ccccc4)n1-2)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n3C. Separately 324 proposals contain an 8- to 11-membered ring and 18 a macrocycle, 309 of those on a single objective, while spiro construction is nearly absent at 12 spiro-containing molecules in 4,350.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-editing operators have no geometric feasibility test, producing transannular aromatic bonds, strained small rings and unconstrained medium rings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring formation, bridging and contraction are validated by valence and canonical identity alone, so the operator set simultaneously produces geometrically impossible bonds and almost never produces the ordinary three-dimensional motif a chemist would reach for. A task-agnostic generator would refuse a new bond between two atoms of the same aromatic ring, bound medium-ring closure to conformationally reasonable sizes, and add explicit spiro and fused-saturated ring construction so that escaping a flat skeleton is a reachable edit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five objectives begin from the same ten initial records, yet basic amine content over 870 proposals ranges from 493 on one objective, where 84 of the 87 best carry one, down to 16 on another where none of the 87 best does; amide content ranges from 677 to 21, urea from 405 to 5, and sulfonamide totals 76 in 4,350 with every occurrence on the objective whose starting set contained one and none in any leader. Aryl halide, by contrast, appears in 834 of 870 proposals on one objective: the cheap class is everywhere and the polar classes are wherever they were inherited.
transferable_gaps.gap: Whole polar and ionisable functional-group classes are reachable only by inheritance from the starting molecules, not by construction.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Entire polar and ionisable group classes are accessible only by inheritance, so a session that drifts away from a class early can never recover it even when the gradient is rewarding exactly that class, and the groups it can install arrive attached to labile atoms. A task-agnostic generator would need operators that install amide, sulfonamide, urea, carboxylic acid, nitrile and basic amine centres de novo onto an existing ring system at rates comparable to its halogen substitution, so group composition is driven by the score rather than by the starting set.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
